locations.description: Five acres of polycarbonate cold-frame glasshouses wrapped in burlap. Steaming compost heaps keep perennial rye seedlings alive in -30°C frost.
Reinforced concrete telephone repeater bunker overlooking the main railway cut. Encircled with concertina wire and claymore firing stakes.
Limestone sluice gates regulating raw saltwater intake from the sound. Massive cast-iron screw pumps caked in white salt crusts.
A 120-meter steel lattice antenna perched on a wind-scoured granite pinnacle. Feeds the automated continental emergency transponder loop.
Four hundred meters deep in dry halite bedrock. Shielded counting chamber forged from pre-1945 armor steel. Contains precision spectrometers.
High-pressure volcanic steam well supplying district heat to the valley. Screaming brass pressure relief valves surrounded by boiling sulfur mud.
Sandbagged concrete bunker with dual heavy machine-gun embrasures. Enforces martial law Schedule 14 grain and diesel levies.
Toxic alluvial swamp where spring meltwater concentrates months of radioactive soot. Deep black mud that dissolves boot stitching.
Heavy timber wharf where the research icebreaker Aurora Borealis maintains auxiliary steam. Shoreline ringed with razor wire.
Underground agricultural research cellar holding dewars of cold-resistant crop roots and heirloom seed flasks.
An eighty-meter depression of glassy green tektite slag where a ground-burst warhead struck. Ringed with cultist prayer flags and iron stakes.
Hundreds of rusted hopper cars and boxcars derailed on frost-heaved tracks. Scavengers pick through grain residues and industrial grease.
Brick pump station housing positive-displacement brass flow meters. Guards in sheepskin coats meter every cubic meter of fresh water.
Geodesic observatory perched above the cloud deck. Houses barometric chart recorders and stratospheric particulate sampling filters.
Concealed steel portal beneath a false limestone outcrop. Contains crated demolition blocks, electric detonators, and one-time pads.
Deep crystalline water basin in an abandoned quarry pit. The water is cold and clear, filtered through fifty feet of porous limestone.
Vertical ladder shaft giving access to buried telecom trunk lines and district heating conduits. Air is damp and smells of sulfur.
Reinforced vehicle shed holding tracked artillery tractors and armored troop carriers with drained radiators.
Wood-fired downdraft brick kiln producing refractory clay blocks for bunker insulation and greenhouse footing construction.
Concrete weigh-station parking lot where northern relief trucks assemble under armed escort for the ice run.
Naturally dry salt room holding thousands of ampoules of antibiotics, freeze-dried blood plasma, and surgical instruments.
Twin concrete arch bridge blown during the early days of the war. A treacherous catwalk of timber and steel cables spans the gap.
Multi-stage flash distillation boiler fueled by coal and peat. Condenses pure drinking water from grey coastal brine.
Two-mile vehicular tunnel blocked by snowdrifts at both portals. Home to eighty displaced miner families living in derelict buses.
Coastal navigation beacon powered by a 90-watt Strontium-90 thermal decay generator. Searing heat keeps the iron roof clear of snow.
River slipway where the ice sheet is graded with sand and salt to permit passage of heavy four-ton supply sleds.
Hardened telecommunications center with banks of dead teletype printers and charred cryptographic key barrels.
Masonry culvert beneath the railway embankment wired with eighty kilograms of plastic explosives wired to automated seismic triggers.
Three interconnected heated domes growing leafy greens, turnips, and medicinal poppies using waste heat from the brickworks.
Shore-fast ice lead where the steel bow of the Aurora Borealis is moored. Gangway watchmen inspect health certificates before boarding.
Subterranean shell foundry inside a hollowed granite dome. Heavy drop hammers forge brass 152mm casing blanks over charcoal hearths.
Locomotive turntable repair shed occupied by armed switchmen. Armored steam handcars are rigged with machine gun mounts.
A zig-zag system of muddy revetted trenches dug directly through radioactive black soil by conscripts wearing burlap respirators.
An underground forty-bed trauma infirmary built in a sterile halite chamber. The air is dry, antiseptic, and completely radiation-free.
A fortified toll gate constructed from overturned refrigerated trailers and diesel fuel tanks. Defended by half-track gunners.
A shattered sixty-foot concrete silo cracked open by a 152mm howitzer shell. Piles of charred, moldering grain smoke in the snow.
Two freight locomotives fused together by intense thermal flash during the Exchange. The surrounding granite ballast is glazed like bottle glass.
Deep limestone vault flooded waist-deep in freezing mineral water. Massive bronze impeller shafts groan under electrical load.
A stagnant bog of yellow, sulfurous runoff from breached pre-war chemical munitions. Heavy vapors pool in shell craters.
Four 152mm heavy field guns dug into log-and-earth revetments. Piles of spent brass cartridge cases glint beneath blowing snow.
A jagged basalt bluff where cultists burn their dead on sulfur-soaked pyres to 'return the bone-ash to the glowing sky.'
A cedar-shingle linesman shed holding banks of wet-cell galvanic batteries and clicking brass telegraph sounders.
An underground peat storage cellar smoldering without flame. Warm, smokey air provides shelter for frostbitten deserters.
Corrugated iron barn storing fifty tons of ammonium nitrate fertilizer bags. Heavily guarded by Works sentries with shotguns.
A cracked concrete bunker whose blast hatch was blown inward by sappers. Skeletal remains frozen in wool coats lie among looted crates.
Stone toll house where water clerks enter cubic-meter withdrawals in leather-bound volumes beside an iron potbelly stove.
Deep buried communications hub with copper-shielded walls. Unmanned teletype banks continuously print automated relay codes.
Massive diesel stone crusher used to produce aggregate for bunker concrete. Sledgehammers and iron chains rust in snowdrifts.
Vast subterranean salt cavern lit by kerosene torches. Scavengers, agronomists, and soldiers trade dried fish and cartridges under neutral truce.
A rusted iron sea buoy frozen fifty yards offshore. Its battery-powered red flasher pulses weakly through dense sea smoke.
A roofless stone belltower offering commanding rifle sightlines over Highway 12. Piles of spent 7.62mm brass litter the spiral stairs.
A steaming pool of scalding volcanic water bubbling up through green impact glass. Emits dense clouds of radon and radioactive steam.
Damp basement under Checkpoint Gamma where deserters and quota defaulters are shackled to iron pipe stanchions.
A massive barricade of felled pine trunks and dry-stone boulders blocking the mountain pass to heavy motor vehicles.
A nine-foot brick sewer arch draining thaw mud from the upper districts. Rushing black water carries debris and discarded gear.
Three burned-out armored halftracks frozen in roadside snowdrifts. Machine-gun holes riddle the steel radiator louvers.
Deep locked room holding forty wooden crates of mining dynamite and copper blasting caps behind a six-inch steel vault door.
Steam-driven maritime foghorn installation. A diesel air compressor groans every two minutes, sounding a low C-flat across the leads.
A sandbagged mortar position overlooking the valley switchbacks. Armed with an 82mm tube zeroed on the rail junction.
A high rocky promontory overlooking the entire thirty-mile valley of Sector 4. The morning sun cuts through clearing stratospheric ash.
A scatter of lean-tos under dead pine, chosen because the canopy still holds enough ash-snow to break a thermal signature. No fire after dark.

A private shelter built into a hillside a decade before the Exchange, its blast door hand-fitted by someone who clearly expected to use it. It has been resupplied every winter since, by nobody the sector can identify.

A repurposed freight depot, its walls papered floor to ceiling with hand-drawn claim maps. Every claimed site is inked in one color; every blacklisted shelter's name is inked in a second color and never crossed out.
A collapsed rail cutting choked with burned-out freight cars, refitted as a den. There is no gate to knock on and no reason to try.
A converted counting house, its walls lined with ledger boxes instead of shelving. Every contract The Tally has ever written is filed here, dated, and enforced on schedule.
A cold former schoolhouse requisitioned for the petition. Testimony taken down in two hands: the petitioner's and the Tally's.
